plain: A programmable machine that can sense its surroundings, decide what to do, and physically act on the world.
snappy: A programmable machine that senses, computes, and acts physically in the world.
detail: A Robot couples Sensing and Perception to Control and Actuation so it can carry out tasks with some Autonomy. Forms range from a fixed Manipulator on a factory line to a mobile Humanoid robot.

plain: The part of a robot that produces movement, like a motor that turns a wheel or bends a joint.
snappy: A device that converts energy into controlled mechanical motion.
detail: An Actuator is the muscle of a robot: an Electric motor, Hydraulic actuator, or Pneumatic actuator that drives a Joint. Its motion is regulated by a Control loop using feedback from an Encoder.

plain: A sensor that scans surroundings with laser pulses to build a 3D map of distances.
snappy: A laser ranging sensor that builds a 3D point cloud of the environment.
detail: LiDAR emits laser pulses and times their return to measure distance, producing a Point cloud used for Perception, SLAM, and Localization. It is a core sensor on many an Autonomous vehicle and Autonomous mobile robot.

plain: Working out the joint angles a robot arm needs so its hand reaches a target spot.
snappy: Computing the joint configuration that places the end-effector at a desired pose.
detail: Inverse kinematics maps a target Pose in task space to Joint angles — the inverse of Forward kinematics. It underpins Motion planning and Manipulation, and can be ill-posed near a Singularity.

plain: A way for a robot to learn skills by trial and error, getting rewards for doing the right thing.
snappy: Learning a control policy by maximizing reward through trial-and-error interaction.
detail: In robotics, Reinforcement learning trains a Policy to choose actions that maximize a Reward function, often in Simulation before Sim-to-real transfer to hardware. It powers learned Locomotion and dexterous Manipulation.
